name: Puthukkulam Sree Nagaraja Temple
tagline: Thodupuzha's rare naga kavu — restored and reorganised after a Deva Prasnam
summary: A rare Nagaraja-centred kavu at Vengalloor (Thodupuzha). The temple is important for Naga rites, Sarpa-dosha remedies and local astrological customs; it was restored after a traditional Deva Prasnam.
description: Puthukkulam Sree Nagaraja Temple at Vengalloor (Manakkad, near Thodupuzha) is one of the uncommon Kerala shrines where Nagaraja (the serpent deity) is the presiding divinity. The complex combines small kavus (sacred groves) and multiple naga shrines alongside a Bhagavathi sanctum.

The temple matters locally as a centre for traditional Naga rites — Noorum Palum, Ashta Naga pooja, Sarpabali and the Ayilyam–Makam festival — and for families seeking remedies for Sarpa Dosha or fertility-related prayers. Devotees from across central Travancore visit on ayilyam days and during the annual Ayilyam Makam mahotsavam.

A decade of neglect gave way to organised revival: a local trust led restoration work and, according to local reports, the rebuilding and re‑installation followed the findings of a traditional Deva Prasnam. The temple reconsecrated parts of the shrine (including the rebuilt illa) in mid‑2025 and now hosts renewed monthly and festival rites.

Visitors find a compact, green setting on Mullackal/Mullackal‑temple road (Thodupuzha), traditional Kerala architecture, and public festival programmes listed in the state tourism '1000 Festivals' directory.
highlights: Nagaraja as the presiding deity — uncommon in Kerala temples
Strong local tradition of Naga rites: Noorum Palum, Ashta Naga pooja, Sarpabali, Makam Idi
Restored and reshaped after a traditional Deva Prasnam; illa (sub‑shrine) reconsecrated in June 2025
Annual Ayilyam–Makam mahotsavam (Kanni / Sep–Oct) with processions and Sarppabali
Easy local access from Vengalloor; listed on Kerala Tourism's 1000 Festivals directory

sections.heading: Background
body: The temple grows from a kavu associated with the old Puthukkulath family and local naga‑worship traditions. Local accounts link the origin story with contacts between Puthukkulath Mana and Pampummekkatt Mana (a noted centre of Naga worship), and the site retains multiple Naga deities and a Bhagavathi shrine.

Over time the kavu fell into partial neglect and a local trust formed to restore the precinct. Reports state that the trust commissioned a traditional Deva Prasnam (astrological ritual consultation) and then carried out rebuilding and reinstallations according to its recommendations.

sections.heading: What to see and do
body: See the tiled‑roof nalambalam, padippura entrance and the open kavu areas with stone serpent pratishthas (Nagaraja, Nagayakshi, Karinaga, Kuzhinaga). The temple retains simple traditional architecture, a namaskara mandapam and an aanapandal for devotees.

Attend monthly Ayilyam observances for Noorum Palum and Ashta Naga rites. The main festival is the Ayilyam–Makam mahotsavam (Kanni, usually Sep–Oct) with processions, Makam Idi distribution and evening Sarppabali; these rites are the focus for families seeking relief from sarpa‑related afflictions.

sections.heading: Plan your visit
body: Best time: attend on the Ayilyam star day each Malayalam month or for the Ayilyam–Makam mahotsavam (Kanni, September–October) for the fullest experience of naga rites. For general darshan, the temple runs daily poojas and special ayilyam observances.

How to reach: the temple is at Vengalloor / Mullackal temple road (Thodupuzha). Vengalloor is about 700 m from the temple according to the Kerala Tourism directory. Nearest airport: Cochin International Airport (≈50 km); nearest major railhead: Aluva (≈51 km). Confirm local bus/parking arrangements before travel.

latest.text: The rebuilt illa (sub‑shrine) that houses core naga pratishthas was ceremonially handed over and consecrated; local reports describe the reconstruction and formal offering ceremony on June 21, 2025.

visitorInfo.bestTime: Ayilyam star days and the Ayilyam–Makam mahotsavam (Kanni, Sep–Oct); monthly Ayilyam observances.
visitorInfo.howToReach: Located in Vengalloor (Mullackal temple road), Thodupuzha; nearest town Vengalloor ~700 m. Nearest airport: Cochin International (~50 km). Nearest major railway: Aluva (~51 km). Local KSRTC and private buses serve Thodupuzha.
etiquette: If you visit for Naga rites or sarpa‑dosha remedies, enquire with the temple office about required offerings and booking — confirm before you travel.
Dress modestly; follow temple routines (first darshan of Ganapati where indicated) and the directions of temple staff during festivals.
Festival days get crowded; arrive early for Ayilyam observances and expect processions and evening Sarppabali rituals.
